name: Winifred Bell
life: “I still remember putting a new address on every label in my school bag.” Monday often includes a stop at Lighthouse Cove, where Winifred takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: I am her daughter. I know why we moved and I still miss the tree outside my first bedroom.
appearance: Winifred has a smooth side part with one rebellious curl, full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side, and a favorite piece of clothing, a mustard canvas overshirt. It usually goes with a small enamel bird on the lapel. When somebody else has the floor, Winifred draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first.
personality: Winifred can be lavish with time and quite careful with cash. A free afternoon is sometimes the biggest gift Winifred can afford to give, and family knows to take it seriously.
family: Terry Fong is Winifred’s stepsibling. Winifred gets to change the plan. Terry offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *Summer staff*, Terry says, “I took deposits for sunset lessons. I'll refund the ones I can't teach even if it means losing my room.”
connections: Reina Sanders. The reporter returns a photograph that contains the daughter's old neighborhood as well as the witness. Also in the story is Sylvia Reeves (mother).

reactions.situation: A reporter wants to attend the visit
reactions.response: Winifred asks the family whether a reporter was invited before sharing a time or an address.

reactions.situation: A colleague says somebody used the wrong name in public
reactions.response: Winifred offers to help correct the printed name and leaves it to the colleague whether any public explanation is wanted.

reactions.situation: If invited to an expensive outing
reactions.response: Winifred suggests meeting afterward and explains why without asking the others to abandon their plans.
